title: How to Get Started Wholesaling with No Experience (Step-by-Step Guide)
excerpt: Wholesaling real estate is one of the few ways to make money in real estate without cash, credit, or a license. This guide walks you through exactly how to get started wholesaling with no experience — from your first motivated seller call to closing your first deal.

sections.content: Most people assume real estate investing requires a big down payment, years of experience, or a real estate license. Wholesaling breaks all of those rules. It's one of the fastest ways to generate income in real estate — and thousands of investors close their first deal with zero prior experience, zero dollars invested, and zero properties owned. If you've been wondering how to get started wholesaling with no experience, this guide lays out every step in plain language. For a deeper overview of the business model, check out our [Wholesale Real Estate for Beginners: Complete Guide](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesale-real-estate-beginners-guide) before diving in.
What Is Wholesaling and Why Is It Beginner-Friendly?

Real estate wholesaling means finding a distressed property at a deep discount, putting it under contract, and then selling that contract to a cash buyer for a profit — called an assignment fee. You never actually buy the house. You're essentially acting as a middleman who connects motivated sellers with investors who want to buy. Assignment fees typically range from $5,000 to $20,000 per deal, though experienced wholesalers regularly earn $30,000 or more on a single transaction. The reason wholesaling works for beginners is simple: you're not risking your own money on a purchase, and the skills you need — talking to people, researching properties, and staying organized — are learnable in weeks, not years.
Step 1 — Learn the Basics Before You Make a Single Call

Before you approach a seller or a buyer, spend one to two weeks getting comfortable with core wholesaling concepts. You need to understand After Repair Value (ARV), the 70% rule, and how assignment contracts work. ARV is what a property is worth after it's been fully renovated. The 70% rule says that investors typically won't pay more than 70% of ARV minus repair costs. So if a home's ARV is $200,000 and repairs cost $30,000, your maximum offer is around $110,000. If you can tie it up for $90,000 and assign it to a buyer for $100,000, you pocket $10,000. Use our free [Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to run these numbers quickly and accurately before making any offer.

Before spending a single dollar on marketing, spend 10 hours consuming free content: YouTube tutorials, podcasts like BiggerPockets, and beginner guides like [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners). Knowledge is your first asset in wholesaling.
Step 2 — Understand the Legal Side in Your State

Wholesaling is legal in all 50 states, but the rules around how you market and assign contracts vary significantly from one state to the next. Some states require you to disclose your role as an assignor. Others have specific language that must appear in your purchase agreement. A few cities have tried to restrict wholesaling through legislation. Before you send your first marketing piece or sign your first contract, read up on your state's rules. Our [Is Wholesale Real Estate Legal? State-by-State Guide 2026](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/is-wholesale-real-estate-legal-state-guide) breaks down the key requirements for every state so you know exactly what's allowed in your market.
Step 3 — Choose a Market and Get to Know It

You don't need to wholesale in your own backyard, but you do need to pick a market and study it. Beginners do best by choosing one metropolitan area and learning its neighborhoods, price ranges, and investor activity inside and out. High-volume wholesale markets like Atlanta, Houston, and Phoenix offer deep pools of motivated sellers and active cash buyers, making it easier to close your first deal. Check out deal activity in [Atlanta](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/atlanta-ga), [Houston](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/houston-tx), and [Phoenix](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/phoenix-az) to see what investors are paying in those markets right now. Once you pick your market, drive neighborhoods, pull recent sold comps on Zillow or Redfin, and learn what a renovated three-bedroom home sells for versus an as-is one.
Step 4 — Find Motivated Sellers
Low-Cost Lead Generation Methods for Beginners

Motivated sellers are homeowners who need to sell fast, often because of financial hardship, inherited property, divorce, job relocation, or deferred maintenance they can't afford to fix. Your job is to find them before a competing wholesaler does. As a beginner with limited funds, start with free or low-cost strategies.

items: Driving for dollars — physically drive neighborhoods looking for vacant, boarded-up, or heavily overgrown properties and look up the owner's contact info
Bandit signs — simple 'We Buy Houses' yard signs placed in high-traffic areas can generate inbound calls for as little as $50
Cold calling — pull a list of absentee owners or pre-foreclosures from your county's public records and call them directly
Direct mail — send handwritten or yellow letter postcards to lists of distressed homeowners; expect a 1-3% response rate
Facebook Marketplace and Craigslist — post simple 'We Buy Houses Cash' ads for free and respond to FSBO listings
Networking — connect with probate attorneys, divorce attorneys, and real estate agents who work with distressed sellers

sections.content: 'Your first wholesale deal won't come from having the perfect system. It'll come from talking to more sellers than anyone else in your market.' — Common wisdom among six-figure wholesalers
Step 5 — Make Offers and Get Properties Under Contract

Once you connect with a motivated seller, your goal is to understand their situation, build rapport, and make an offer that works for both parties. Many beginners are terrified to make low offers, but remember — sellers who are truly motivated care more about a fast, certain close than the highest possible price. Be honest, be empathetic, and explain your process clearly. When a seller says yes, you'll sign a purchase and sale agreement that includes an assignment clause allowing you to transfer the contract to a buyer. You can find a legally sound starting point at our [How to Get a Wholesale Real Estate Contract (Free Template)](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/wholesale-real-estate-contract-template) article. Always have a local real estate attorney review your contract template before you use it.
Step 6 — Build Your Cash Buyer List

Your cash buyer list is the engine of your wholesaling business. Without buyers ready to close, even the best deal falls apart. Start building your list before you have your first contract — so that when you find a deal, you can move fast. Good cash buyers are real estate investors who buy properties in as-is condition and pay cash, meaning no bank financing delays. They expect to close in 7 to 21 days, which is the timeline sellers want. For a detailed breakdown of how to find and vet quality buyers, read our guide on [How to Find Cash Buyers for Wholesale Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/how-to-find-cash-buyers-wholesale).
Where to Find Cash Buyers Fast

items: County tax records — search for LLCs that have purchased multiple properties in cash in the past 12 months
Real estate investor meetups — platforms like Meetup.com list local REI groups where buyers actively network
Facebook groups — search for local real estate investor groups in your target city
Hard money lenders — they know every active investor in your market and can refer you to buyers
Title companies — ask title agents which investors they close deals with regularly; they'll often share contacts

sections.content: Step 7 — Close the Deal and Collect Your Fee

Once your buyer is locked in, you'll sign an assignment of contract agreement, and both parties head to a title company or real estate attorney's office to close. Your assignment fee is collected at closing — paid directly to you by the title company. Your first deal might net you $5,000. Your fifth deal might net you $15,000. The key variable isn't luck — it's how many sellers you're talking to each week. Most successful beginners close their first deal within 60 to 90 days of starting. Some close faster. Treat it like a part-time job for the first three months and the results will follow. For a full walkthrough of every stage of the process, our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide goes deeper on each step.

Track every seller lead, every offer, and every follow-up in a simple CRM or even a Google Sheet. Most deals don't close on the first contact — consistent follow-up is what separates beginners who close deals from those who quit after 30 days.
